dialect.guess: GnuCOBOL (OpenCOBOL) or similar open-source COBOL on Linux
evidence: Project 'ORCA' - JMA (Japan Medical Association) open source medical software
No EXEC SQL, no EXEC CICS, no COMP-3

purpose.summary: This is a subprogram (ORCS02) that calculates patient co-payment amounts for inpatient medical billing, part of the JMA (Japan Medical Association) ORCA standard receipt software system. It handles complex Japanese health insurance co-payment calculations including public assistance (Kohi), self-pay, and various regional subsidy schemes.

notable_features: Japanese-language comments encoded in latin-1 (EUC-JP or Shift-JIS garbled)
No EXEC SQL or EXEC CICS
No COMP-3 packed decimal despite financial calculations
87 CALL statements indicating heavy use of subprogram architecture
283 PERFORM statements indicating structured procedural decomposition
OCCURS tables for daily/monthly insurance co-payment tracking (up to 31 days)
Open source JMA ORCA medical receipt software (copyright 2002)
Extensive revision history in comments spanning 2002-2005
verdict.notes: File decoded with latin-1 but contains Japanese text (likely EUC-JP or Shift-JIS), causing mojibake in the comments. The program is clearly production medical billing software from the JMA ORCA project. The absence of COMP-3 is somewhat unusual for financial COBOL but consistent with some GnuCOBOL/OpenCOBOL implementations. The 508KB size and 10,064 lines confirm a substantial production subprogram.
